summary: Android renders a different screen/state: a full-width "Create Agent" modal over a dimmed charcoal backdrop, while React renders the "Meet Cindy" onboarding panel.

Android omits React's onboarding elements: "Set up your server", the large "Meet Cindy" title, introduction, pixel-art Cindy card, centered description, runtime helper text, disabled "Create Cindy" button, and footer links.

Android adds form elements absent from React: a close icon, header Create button, warning triangle, populated Computer and Name fields, Description textarea, character counter, runtime-unavailable notice, and populated Runtime selector.

Warning and control styling differ: React bolds "Upgrade for more" and shows a runtime refresh icon, whereas Android adds a warning icon and uses regular-weight upgrade copy.

Android and React use separate component variants and flow states instead of a shared create-agent onboarding contract.

Platform-specific typography, spacing, and component styling were not aligned.

summary: Component bounds differ: React fills the 390×844 viewport edge-to-edge, while Android uses a smaller centered rounded modal over a dark gray scrim.
